title: Vesper and the Verdict
premise: Estate lawyer Sebastian Vane is summoned to Blackthorn Grange to read the will of Edith Marlowe, a woman declared dead seven years ago — and the will insists she died only last week. Twin letters arrive: one confessing to her original 'death,' one promising the truth of who buried her alive in paperwork, if not in fact. As Sebastian untangles a forged death certificate, a disinherited nephew, and a housekeeper who never left, they discover Edith staged her disappearance to test which of her heirs would kill to keep the inheritance. In the end, Sebastian must choose between loyalty to the client who hired them and the truth that convicts the one person who showed them kindness — and the verdict they deliver decides whether Blackthorn Grange, and its last living secret, survives.
about_author: Oscar Reyes is a former probate clerk who spent a decade watching families come apart over paper. He writes mysteries about the lies documents tell, from a coastal town that resembles no town in particular.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Sebastian Vane arrives at rain-soaked Blackthorn Grange to execute Edith Marlowe's will, only to find her death certificate dated seven years ago — and a fresh will signed last month. The housekeeper, Ruth, watches Sebastian too closely. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: unease, the professional's confidence cracking as the paperwork refuses to add up.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Two sealed letters surface in Edith's desk, addressed to Sebastian by name: one confesses she faked her death to escape her husband; the other, in different ink, promises 'the rest of it' if Sebastian reopens the case before the estate settles Friday. The disinherited nephew, Callum, threatens litigation — and knows things he shouldn't. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: complicity and dread; Sebastian realizes they've been chosen, not hired.

chapters.title: What Ruth Buried
chapters.summary: Sebastian digs into the original death and finds Ruth's fingerprints all over the forged certificate — and a hospital record showing Edith alive three years after her funeral. Confronted, Ruth admits she helped Edith vanish but swears the second letter isn't Edith's hand. Then Callum is found unconscious in the east wing, and the Friday deadline burns down to hours. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: loyalty fracturing; the person Sebastian trusted most is the likeliest liar.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Sebastian stages the will reading as a trap, forcing the true author of the second letter to reveal themselves: Ruth, who kept Edith captive to control the estate, and killed her when the first letter slipped out. Sebastian must read the real will aloud — which leaves everything to Ruth, the woman who confessed — or declare it void and let the truth destroy the only home Edith's heirs have left. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: costly resolution; truth wins, belonging doesn't, and Sebastian signs the verdict anyway.
